reviews.body:
One concern: this change can completely eliminate jitter once the exponential backoff exceeds the configured maximum by enough.

For example, in the new test, the base delay is 800ms and jitter produces values between 640ms and 960ms. All values are capped to exactly 150ms, so every retry gets the same delay.

This could cause multiple clients to retry in sync during an outage, which defeats the purpose of jitter.

Is this trade-off intentional? If possible, we should preserve some randomness while ensuring the final delay never exceeds `maxIntervalMs`.

comments.body:
Good point, and yes: once the backoff is far enough past `maxIntervalMs`, every client gets exactly that value. I noted this in the description; it follows the Java SDK's `BackoffThrottler`, which also takes the minimum after applying jitter.

If keeping some spread at the cap is preferred, one option is `min(max, min(max, backoff) * jitter)`: it never exceeds the maximum, and with the default jitter about half of the saturated delays would fall between 80% and 100% of it (the rest at exactly the maximum). I can switch to that if the maintainers would rather have it.

_This was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code)._
